# Part 05 — bench policy annex

This volume documents bench policy annex for the bench flux reactor program. Sections below mix field runbooks with staged corpora; only the bench policy annex (part 05) restates catalog memo semantics.

## 1.0 Scope — bench policy annex

### 1.001

On corpora with forked levels audit cell 1.001 under bench annex supersedes SCN-Alpha seed rows while measuring schema_version markers; empty rule rosters may accept illegal edge jumps. When auditing corpora the runbook asks operators to walk gate ranks in ascending priority without skipping corner_cap and to log bench scenario ids in the intake packet. Ticket FLUX-1001 cross-links stable_needed telemetry with sqlite_busy samples and stable_streak annotations from the prior shift.

**Regression patterns tied to bench annex** — pass 1.001 validates catalog revision markers only after walk gate ranks in ascending priority without skipping corner_cap; Historically vent lag alarms telemetry must not override catalog memo semantics during matrix replay for database lock avoidance. Ticket FLUX-1001 cross-links tick_index telemetry with init_workspace samples and stable_needed annotations from the prior shift.

## Annex index — authoritative bench policy rules

The entries below restate catalog memo semantics for `/app/var/game.db` grading. Informal field bulletins are non-authoritative.

### B2.001

Fresh installs must record catalog revision B2 in meta under key schema_version with string value 2. Archive drafts referencing B1 indicate incomplete materialization.

### B2.002

Initialization copies all nine chamber rows from the scenario seed. Companion components rows must bind level from the seed cell level field, not from grid row ordinals or column indices.

### B2.003

Each scenario requires three constraints rows — one per kind (pump, rod, vent) — carrying min_level and max_level copied from the seed constraints table.

### B2.004

Ranked rules rows must be present after init with priorities 10, 20, and 30 for the standard SCN-Alpha roster. An empty roster causes move acceptance to become permissive.

### GL.001

Move gates execute in ascending priority rank (lower number first). The SCN-Alpha roster uses adjacency_delta at rank 10, corner_cap at rank 20, and type_max at rank 30.

### GL.002

Edge-kind coupling considers only edge-adjacent cells (Manhattan distance 1). Diagonal neighbors never couple.

### GL.003

Among edge neighbors sharing the same kind, let delta equal the absolute difference between proposed level and neighbor level. Reject when delta is strictly greater than param_a; delta equal to param_a is permitted when the band width is one.

### GL.004

Corner envelope cells (0,0), (0,2), (2,0), and (2,2) may not exceed param_a. SCN-Alpha uses envelope 2.

### GL.005

Illegal moves must not mutate components. Metrics change only after tick.

### DO.001

After each tick, compare metric_a, metric_b, and metric_c against inclusive band windows on the scenario row. All three must be in band simultaneously for the tick to count as stable.

### DO.002

The session stable_streak field is the dwell counter. It increments by one on stable ticks and resets to zero when any metric leaves band. It must not increment on set alone.

### DO.003

Victory requires dwell counter greater than or equal to stable_needed from the scenario row. SCN-Alpha uses stable_needed 3.

### DO.004

Loss fires when any metric is greater than or equal to loss columns from the scenario row. Do not compare against band upper bounds for loss.

### SA.001

Save copies the active row into a named slot. Load restores tick index, metric triple, dwell counter, and component levels via slot_levels snapshot.

### SA.002

When archiving levels, read all component rows into memory before writing slot_levels rows. Interleaving an open read cursor with writes on the same connection can surface database is locked and truncate streak or level snapshots.
